items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I have a lot of records by Coltrane and I listen to Coltrane.

ctx.x: faster. And the more faster it got, the more improvisations he put on it. And it was just like taking a saxophone lesson listening to him play this. He was marvelous musician.

But, see, I went more for the Benny Carter type of playing because Benny had the -- I always like the sound, I like a certain sound. Although, right now I still -- I listen to Don Byas and I hear a lot of Bird's passages now that Don plays. But he had the sound that was such a warm musical sound that it makes it -- I have a lot of records by Coltrane and I listen to Coltrane. He sounded like a beginner when you listen to Don Byas afterwards, although he was great. Great saxophone player but none of them go for…
Well, would you say Sonny Rollins has more of a sound?
